spectral.true_color: High confidence: orange-brown and muted tan surfaces dominate illuminated terrain, with discrete green patches and extensive near-black zones. Surface brightness changes sharply across several diagonal boundaries.
spectral.false_color: High confidence: the green patches become bright pink-red, particularly in top_center, middle_left and middle_center. The bottom_center patch is a more muted red. Much of the brown background becomes olive, tan or gray-green, while the darkest zones remain dark.

implications.claim: The green-to-red correspondence identifies localized photosynthetically active vegetation.
Red intensity varies with vegetation amount or condition, but illumination, canopy structure and rendering also contribute; relative physiological vigor is not securely measurable.
The widespread brown and weakly red background is consistent with exposed mineral surfaces, dry vegetation or a mixture of both.
Vegetation concentrated in strips and pockets may reflect locally greater moisture availability or deeper soil.
Terrain shadow is the leading explanation for the broad dark zones, given their banded configuration and adjoining rough slopes.
Open water is not confidently identified, so water turbidity cannot be assessed.
No coherent built-surface pattern is resolved; isolated structures could remain undetected.

spectral.not_revealed: High confidence: these displayed composites cannot provide calibrated reflectance, quantitative vegetation indices, soil moisture, vegetation species, crop identity, canopy height, water depth or temperature. They also cannot establish temporal change, management history, exact season or climate.

summaries.w25: Rugged, mostly brown terrain contains scattered active vegetation and broad dark bands, probably terrain shadows. Landscape interpretation has medium confidence; vegetation identification has high confidence.
summaries.w50: The patch likely shows rugged, sparsely vegetated terrain with extensive terrain shadow; medium confidence. Approximate visible fractions are 56% brown surfaces, 12% green vegetation and 32% obscured dark terrain. Green patches become red in false color; high confidence. Water, agriculture and settlement are not securely identified.
summaries.w100: The patch likely depicts rugged terrain dominated by exposed or sparsely vegetated brown surfaces; medium confidence. Estimated visible fractions are 56% brown terrain, 12% green vegetation and 32% dark, obscured terrain. A broad southwest–northeast dark corridor and subsidiary bands probably reflect terrain shadow; medium confidence. Green patches in the upper center, middle left and lower center become red in false color, confirming localized active vegetation; high confidence. No convincing parcel grid, road network or settlement is resolved. Season, biome, moisture status and active land management remain uncertain.
summaries.w200:
The 1.2 km patch likely contains rugged, sparsely vegetated terrain with extensive terrain shadow; medium confidence. Approximate visible fractions are 56% brown exposed or sparsely vegetated surfaces, 12% distinct green vegetation and 32% dark, obscured terrain. These are appearance estimates, and shadow conceals underlying cover.

A broad dark corridor crosses southwest–northeast through the middle, with additional diagonal bands and a southward lobe on the right. Their association with rough brown surfaces favors terrain-controlled illumination; medium confidence. Vegetation occurs as a bent strip in the upper center, a compact patch at middle left, smaller central patches and a larger patch near the lower center. Their green true-color appearance and red false-color response identify active vegetation with high confidence.

Irregular vegetation pockets may indicate locally favorable moisture or soil conditions; low confidence. No convincing agricultural parcel pattern, road network or settlement is resolved; medium confidence. Water is not confidently identified, preventing turbidity assessment. Exact season, vegetation type, climate and active processes such as irrigation, harvesting, flooding or clearing cannot be established from these renderings.
summaries.w400:
The patch most likely represents rugged terrain dominated by exposed rock or soil and sparse vegetation; medium confidence. Estimated appearance fractions are 56% brown exposed or sparsely vegetated surfaces, 12% distinct green vegetation and 32% dark, obscured terrain. These approximate fractions describe what is visible; shadow is not an underlying land-cover class.

The strongest spatial feature is a broad southwest–northeast dark corridor crossing the central area and reaching the western and eastern margins. Additional northwest–southeast dark bands occur on the left, while an elongated dark lobe occupies much of the lower right. Rough adjoining surfaces, irregular boundaries and repeated banding favor terrain shadow as the main explanation; medium confidence. Water cannot be excluded from every dark pixel, but no water body is securely identified.

Vegetation is concentrated in a bent upper-center strip approximately 280–330 m long, a roughly 170 × 130 m patch at middle left, smaller patches along the central dark boundary, and an approximately 160 × 150 m patch near the lower center. Narrow vegetation streaks also occur in the upper right. Their green true-color appearance and pink-red false-color response provide high-confidence evidence of localized active vegetation. The surrounding weakly red, brown terrain is consistent with mineral surfaces mixed with dry or sparse vegetation; medium confidence.

Vegetation pockets could reflect sheltered positions, deeper soils or greater moisture availability, but that explanation has low confidence. Red intensity alone cannot isolate plant vigor from canopy cover, illumination and display effects. A dry, rocky upland setting is plausible at low confidence; a particular biome, climate or season is unresolved.

No convincing parcel grid, planting rows, road network, building cluster or forestry clearing is apparent; medium confidence. Crop identity, rotation, irrigation, harvesting, flooding and recent clearing cannot be established. Apparent terrain dissection may reflect erosion, but active sediment movement is not demonstrated. At 10 m resolution, narrow channels, tracks, small structures and vegetation types remain uncertain. Display upsampling adds no spatial detail, and the two composites cannot supply quantitative moisture, elevation, canopy height or temporal change.
